## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.13 — One root cause behind most of it, plus recording

> **Alpha.** Fixes the issues found using alpha.12 on a real phone, and adds
> the two features alpha.12 deliberately left. The Kotlin in this build has
> never been compiled anywhere but CI.

### The app kept leaving its own shell

Most of the "it re-initialises whenever I navigate" behaviour was one bug
wearing several hats.

HueMux is an iframe shell: switching tabs is a visibility toggle, not a
navigation, which is what keeps a running screen capture and each page's
WebSocket alive while you look at something else. Two routes led out of it.

Settings was a plain link rather than a frame, so tapping it navigated the top
window and destroyed every iframe. From that point on there was no shell at
all, and every later tab switch was a full page load that refetched and
re-rendered from an empty view. And separately, the shell rewrites the address
bar to the current tab's page — so a reload, or a WebView restored by the
system, resolved to that page directly, outside the shell, with nothing to put
it back.

Settings is now a third frame, the brand link no longer points out of the
shell, and a directly-loaded page redirects back into it. `?standalone=1` opts
out when you want one page on its own.

This is also why a reloaded sync page offered "Start" for a stream that was
already running: the capture service outlives a WebView reload. The controls
now read the server's stream state as well as the page's own.

### Lights

- **No more flash of "No lights found on this bridge."** The grid was gated
  behind a socket connecting, reporting `paired`, and four fetches resolving,
  and drew an empty state while it waited. The last known lights, rooms, scenes
  and favourites are now cached and painted immediately, and the empty state is
  only drawn once the server has actually answered — an empty list before the
  first fetch is not a conclusion.
- **The room list is no longer cut off.** It had become a bottom sheet, which
  put it at the opposite end of the screen from the finger that opened it,
  implied a modality it did not have, and sat underneath the fixed bottom nav,
  which silently ate the last rows of a long list. It is now full-width with
  finger-sized rows, anchored directly below the control that opens it, and
  dismissed by tapping anywhere, pressing Escape, or picking something.

### Theme

**Palette and visual effects are two buttons now.** They were one five-state
cycle — system, light, dark, simple-light, simple-dark — behind a single
button, so getting back where you started took five taps through icons that
differed only by how much of a crescent was lit. They are independent: "simple"
is any palette with the decorative layers removed. A device that stored one of
the old combined values is migrated rather than reset.

Start, Stop and Change source no longer all appear at once, either.

### New: capture resolution and screen recording

**Capture resolution** is now a slider rather than a fixed value, showing the
size it actually produces. Raising it buys nothing for sync itself — the colour
pipeline reduces everything to a 64×36 grid — so it is there for recording;
turn it back down afterwards, because a bigger mirror costs battery
continuously. The default is unchanged in cost: a typical 1080×2400 phone still
captures at a 480-pixel long edge.

**Screen recording** writes an MP4 to Movies/HueMux while sync runs, at either
of two qualities:

- **Match capture** — the same size the pipeline samples. Cheap, and shows what
  the sync engine was reacting to. This is the default.
- **Full resolution** — the display's own resolution. A better video, and a
  second full-size encode.

Worth knowing: recording always needs a second screen mirror of its own.
Android binds a mirror to exactly one destination for its lifetime, and this
one's is already the colour pipeline — so the quality setting picks that second
mirror's resolution, not whether it exists. A device that refuses a second
mirror loses recording and keeps syncing; it will say so rather than failing
quietly.

### Verified, and not

Driven in a browser against a real bridge, read-only: the shell survives a lap
through all three tabs with its frames' sockets intact, the lights grid paints
from cache with the empty state never appearing, the dropdown opens and
dismisses correctly, and the theme migration produces the right result. Go
build, vet, tests and the android/arm64 cross-build are clean.

Nothing Android-specific is verified. This host has no Android SDK, so the new
Kotlin — the recorder, the capture-scale plumbing, the bridge methods — is
compiled for the first time by CI and run for the first time by you. Recording
in particular touches parts of MediaProjection that vary by manufacturer. If it
misbehaves, Settings → Diagnostics is the fastest way to say how.
